blindSummary:
This unit contains two of the country's six highest-victim regions in the national 2012-2025 monitoring dataset, and multiple documented public-space incidents directly relevant to a traveller: a homophobic assault in a deprived district of one of the country's largest cities (March 2025), cited as part of a regional-rights body's finding of a "troubling increase in the geographic spread" of bias violence; and a verbal attack culminating in threats of stabbing against an LGBTQ-rights activist at a railway station in a town of the unit (October 2025) - a public transit setting any visitor could encounter. A kidnapping with violence and robbery occurred in another city of the unit (May 2024), though the mobile police unit's swift intervention drew public commendation from the same rights organisation.

Two of the unit's cities hosted Pride marches in 2025, indicating continued public LGBTQ presence. No area of the country with special legislative autonomy used its expanded competence against transgender people. There are no criminal facility bans or enforcement mechanisms targeting visitors. The violence is criminal and street-level, not state-imposed, but its concentration and public-transit exposure raise the probability of encounter for a traveller.

On balance, two high-victim regions plus railway-station and street incidents place this unit's practical risk above the country average. It lacks the landmark positive judicial response recorded in one neighbouring unit and carries more public-space exposure; its position is close to another unit whose qualitative pattern is heavier - documented suicides and sustained rising bullying rather than concentrated victim counts.
